column1: Binary Tree Right Side View — return the values of nodes visible from the right side of the tree, ordered top to bottom. Example: [1,2,3,null,5,null,4] → [1,3,4].
column2: PATTERN: BFS, take last node per level. | INSIGHT: At each level, only the rightmost node is visible from the right. | STEPS: 1) ans=[], q=deque([root]) (skip if root None). 2) While q: n=len(q); for i in range(n): node=q.popleft(); if i==n-1: ans.append(node.val); enqueue children. 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(width). | PITFALL: A right-only DFS fails when a left subtree extends deeper than the right.

column1: Average of Levels in Binary Tree — return list of average values per level. Example: [3,9,20,null,null,15,7] → [3.0, 14.5, 11.0].
column2: PATTERN: BFS level sweep. | INSIGHT: Sum and count per level → average. | STEPS: 1) ans=[], q=deque([root]). 2) While q: n=len(q); s=0; for _ in range(n): node=q.popleft(); s+=node.val; enqueue children. ans.append(s/n). 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(width). | PITFALL: Use float division; large sums may overflow other languages (Python is fine).

column1: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal — return values level by level as a list of lists. Example: [3,9,20,null,null,15,7] → [[3],[9,20],[15,7]].
column2: PATTERN: BFS with per-level grouping. | INSIGHT: Capture queue size BEFORE the inner loop to lock the level boundary. | STEPS: 1) ans=[], q=deque([root]) (skip if root None). 2) While q: level=[]; for _ in range(len(q)): node=q.popleft(); level.append(node.val); enqueue children. ans.append(level). 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(width). | PITFALL: Snapshotting len(q) once per level is what defines the level boundary.

column1: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal — return level order but alternating direction (level 0 L→R, level 1 R→L, ...). Example: [3,9,20,null,null,15,7] → [[3],[20,9],[15,7]].
column2: PATTERN: BFS level + reverse alternate levels. | INSIGHT: Same as level order; reverse the level list when depth is odd (or use a deque with appendleft). | STEPS: 1) Standard BFS level order. 2) Track depth; if depth%2==1: level.reverse() before appending. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(width). | PITFALL: Don't reverse the queue traversal direction itself — only the OUTPUT for that level.
